_about: THE HORSE FRAME: one body plan at one metre-scale, which every horse-shaped animal stands on. `s` is the whole animal's size (1 = a 1.6m horse at the withers), so a zebra is this frame at .85 and a pony at .75. Everything below is written in terms of it, which is what makes the frame a frame.
_headScale: the head cluster -- skull, muzzle, nose, ears, eyes -- shrunk about the neck joint (mammals.js)
_lobes: rump and chest: [x, y, z, half-length, half-height, half-width]. The torso is swept as one chain between them (mammals.js)

thorns._about: the mane in thorns (manes.js): a CREST of locks along the top of the neck to the poll, falling back and to one side

_proportions: 2026-10-24: the head a WEDGE (the muzzle a tapered pill from inside the skull to the nose, its colour near the body's), the neck deep where it leaves the chest, the hind thigh full (thigh 1.5), round hooves, a full tail (it widens as its hair falls); the trunk shorter and shallower (as long as the horse is tall at the withers, the belly ~.86 s up)
